## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Rūpiyasaṁvohāra* Sutta constitutes the nineteenth rule in the *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* within the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text sets forth the disciplinary injunction concerning commercial transactions involving currency, establishing that a Buddhist monk who receives money through trading incurs an offense that requires relinquishing the proceeds and making a formal confession (*nissaggiya pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
This disciplinary rule is widely paralleled across the Vinaya traditions of other early Buddhist schools, including extant Vibhaṅga and Prātimokṣa texts of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya lineages preserved in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan, as well as the corresponding monastic code for nuns (such as Pali *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya* 22) and the *Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies substantial Pali-internal text reuse (775 matching passages across 138 texts), highlighting extensive shared legal and narrative phraseology with Khandhaka chapters—most prominently the *Senāsanakkhandhaka* (Kd 16), *Cīvarakkhandhaka* (Kd 8), and *Samathakkhandhaka* (Kd 14)—adjacent Vibhaṅga rules such as *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* 18 and 22, and later commentarial texts including the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* and *Vinayālaṅkāra-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments by DharmaNexus also match procedural passages in Tibetan Vinaya treatises, including the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) and the *Ekottarakarmaśataka* (D4118) [DharmaNexus].
